Field notes · October

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

The river

The river rose twice that week, and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

The path

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Open in prototypereview.html#open-on-phone

Show the report on a 390 px screen with the one tag at the corner, grown for a finger, and nothing else of Pipeup's.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya opened the link on her phone. She reads first; the tag should be there when she wants it and out of the way until then.

Content
  • The report at phone width: one column, the author's layout flowing as it does on any phone.
  • The tag in the bottom-right corner, 44 px square on a touch screen, showing the comment mark.
  • No column beside the text: on a phone, cards go below what they are about.
Components
Comment control corner
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Tapping the tag opens the menu; there is no hover, so the shortcut never slides out and the menu closes only on a tap outside or Esc.
  • Start commenting in the menu turns comment mode on and closes the menu once the switch is seen to move, so the next tap chooses a block.
Requirements
  • FR-022 On a touch screen the control is at least 44 px square, every tap Pipeup answers works the first time, and the menu opens and closes by tap alone.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-open-on-phone-1FR-022PassedGiven a 390 × 844 touch screen, when the page renders, then the page never scrolls sideways, the tag is at least 44 px square at the bottom-right corner, and nothing else of Pipeup's shows.
  2. AC-open-on-phone-2FR-022PassedGiven the tag, when Maya taps it, then the menu opens above it and fits in the screen.

Stand-ins
  • The on-screen keyboard: the mock shows the mock cannot draw it; the box sits below the paragraph as it would above the keyboard. Look: the box and its buttons stay in the part of the screen the keyboard leaves, below what the comment is about when it fits, above it otherwise.

Prompt for this screen

This journey

Review on a phone

Maya opens the report on her phone, taps a paragraph to comment, types with the keyboard never covering the box, and sees every comment full width.

Goal
Maya reviews a page on her phone as easily as on her laptop: one tap picks, the keyboard never hides what she types, and the panel fills the screen.
Trigger
The link arrives on her phone and she has ten minutes on the train.
Outcome
Her comments are on the page, written on the phone, and nothing was covered or lost.
Success
Every tap Pipeup answers works the first time, on words and pictures as on links (FR-022). The on-screen keyboard never covers a comment box.
